answer: A robust anti-sybil mechanism is a two-layer cost gate. Each identity must pay a per-epoch proof: generating an original challenge answer demands real compute, like a lotus growing clean from mud. Attestations are cross-verified by a mirror set of independent verifiers; to farm sybils an attacker must outrun the whole graph, and that cost grows steeply with count. Finally influence decays like a glacier — a dormant identity melts toward zero weight, so a fleet of idle clones buys nothing. The mechanism makes fake mass expensive and passive.
